info.name: Get-Rescue APIs
info.description:
Ticket search and ticket create/update for the Get-Rescue Zoho Creator app.

## Before you start

Set the collection variables (Collection > Variables):

- `searchKey` — already filled in, the public key for searchTickets
- `createKey` — already filled in, the public key for createTicket

## How Creator Custom APIs behave

Each API is registered in Zoho with ONE HTTP method, and that choice decides where parameters go:

- **GET** — parameters go in the query string (searchTickets works this way)
- **POST** — parameters go in the JSON body, and query-string parameters are IGNORED

If a request returns `9400 The provided HTTP method is not valid for this custom API`, the API is registered with the other method. Swap it and move the parameters accordingly.

## Reading the response

Every response is wrapped by Creator:

```json
{ "result": "<a JSON string>", "code": 3000 }
```

The outer `code: 3000` only means Creator ran the script. **Parse `result` and read the inner `code`** — that is the real outcome. The tests in this collection do exactly that.

## Verified

Every request here was run against the live APIs on 28 September 2026. searchTickets is registered as **GET**, createTicket as **POST** — that is measured, not assumed.

item.name: Search Tickets
item.description:
One search term is tried against seven fields. Registered as GET, so parameters go in the query string.

| Field | Match |
| --- | --- |
| Case ID | as sent |
| Vehicle registration | as sent |
| Client tracking ID | as sent |
| Customer name | as sent |
| UCID | as sent |
| Phone number | last 10 digits |
| Caller ID | last 10 digits |

Phone and caller ID match on the last ten digits, so `+91 72100 36790`, `07210036790` and `7210036790` all find the same ticket.

query.description: Any of the seven searchable values. Minimum 3 characters.

request.description: Verified live: returns the most recent tickets carrying this number, newest first.
A full Case ID returns exactly that ticket. A partial one (`RSID711`) returns every ticket whose ID contains it.

UCID matches the term exactly as sent, not on the last ten digits — it is a 17-digit Ozonetel call id, and trimming it would match the wrong ticket.

NOTE: the `UCID` and `callerID` fields on Create_Case are new and nothing populates them yet, so this returns NO_MATCH until a ticket is created carrying call details.
Returns `result: NO_MATCH` with an empty array. A search that finds nothing is a SUCCESS, not an error — check `result`, not just `code`.
Fewer than 3 characters is refused with `QUERY_TOO_SHORT`. A one or two character term matches most of the table and is never what the caller intended.

item.name: Create / Update Ticket
item.description:
One API does both. Omit `recordId` to create; supply it to update.

**Set the `createKey` collection variable before running these.**

If these return `9400`, the API is registered as GET rather than POST — move the body fields into the query string.

request.description:
Creates a Create_Case record and returns `mode: created` with the new `recordId` and `caseId`.

**Required:** customerName, mobile, vehicle, issue.
**Optional:** email, callerID, ucid.

**vehicle** — either a Vehicle Master record ID, or the vehicle name exactly as it appears there (case does not matter).

**issue** — either a Vehicle Issue record ID, or the issue name. Several may be sent comma-separated. If any resolves to a TOW-type issue the ticket is created as TOW, otherwise RSR.

**callerID / ucid** — the telephony details of the call this ticket came from. Both are optional; omit them for a ticket raised any other way. They are echoed back in the response so you can confirm what was stored, and both become searchable through the searchTickets API.

A value still containing a placeholder such as `$CallerID$` is treated as absent and stored blank — storing that literal text would make the ticket look like it came from a call it did not.

The four required fields and nothing else. `email`, `callerID` and `ucid` are all optional — omitting them is the normal case for a ticket raised from WhatsApp or the website rather than a phone call.

Use this to confirm the API still behaves for callers that predate the telephony fields.

Supplying `recordId` switches the API to update mode. Returns `mode: updated` and `updatedFields`.

**Only the fields you send are changed** — everything else on the ticket is left alone. Send at least one of customerName, mobile, email, vehicle or issue.

A `recordId` that does not exist is refused, and nothing is created or updated.

item.name: Attach call details to an existing ticket

request.description:
The main reason `callerID` and `ucid` exist: a ticket was raised first, and the call it came from is linked afterwards.

Only the two fields sent are changed — the customer, vehicle, issue and everything else on the ticket are left exactly as they were. The response lists what changed in `updatedFields`.

Once attached, `searchTickets` finds this ticket by either value.

Writes nothing. Useful as a setup check:

- `"recordId 1 was supplied but no Create_Case record with that ID exists"` — the recordId parameter IS registered, update mode works
- `"Customer Name is required"` — recordId is NOT registered on the Custom API screen, so it arrived null and the call fell through to create mode

Both values are rejected and stored blank rather than written literally.

This is not hypothetical: Ozonetel's ScreenPop sends its own tokens unsubstituted when misconfigured, and this project has hit exactly that. A ticket carrying the literal text `$CallerID$` would look like it came from a call it did not, and would never be found by any real search.

Expect `updatedFields` to come back empty, or an error saying no field was supplied to change — both mean the guard fired correctly.

exec: // Creator wraps every reply as { result: "<json string>", code: 3000 }.
// The outer code only means the script RAN — the real outcome is inside.
catch (e) { pm.test('Response is JSON', () => { throw new Error('Not JSON: ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 200)); }); }
